title: S&P DJI September quarterly rebalance takes effect at the open — S&P 500/100/400/600 membership and float changes, implemented at the 2026-09-18 close
source: NEWS: press.spglobal.com release dated 2026-09-04, "Bloom Energy, Illumina, and Everpure Set to Join S&P 500; Others to Join S&P 100, S&P MidCap 400, and S&P SmallCap 600", fetched direct 2026-09-08 (HTTP 200). Its effective-date wording is verbatim: changes take place "effective prior to the open of trading on Monday, September 21, 2026, to coincide with the quarterly rebalance". Named S&P 500 changes: Bloom Energy (BE) replaces Molson Coors Beverage (TAP), Everpure (P) replaces The Trade Desk (TTD), Illumina (ILMN) replaces Builders FirstSource (BLDR); S&P 100 adds Dell (DELL), Palo Alto Networks (PANW), Arista (ANET) and Sandisk (SNDK), removing Honeywell Aerospace (HONA), NIKE (NKE), Simon Property (SPG) and Colgate-Palmolive (CL). Filed estimate on the two limits this lane has recorded before: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has no member for an index owner's own published schedule (the same gap russell-quarterly-ipo-review-effective-2026-09-21 and every Russell entry record), and a discovering sweep may not self-confirm an event it found in-sweep. The DATE IS THE OWNER'S OWN and is not in doubt — the estimate label is about the taxonomy, not the evidence
notes: Proposed by the opex-2026-09-18 pulse-check adjacency sweep (2026-09-08). WHY IT IS A SEPARATE ENTRY FROM WHAT IS ALREADY TRACKED: the calendar carries the ANNOUNCEMENT (sp-rebalance-proforma-2026-09-04) and the CAPPED pro-forma (sp-rebalance-proforma-2026-09-11) but not the effective date the owner actually published, which is the third and last milestone of the same quarterly cycle. WHY IT MATTERS TO OPEX-2026-09-18 AND NOTHING ELSE: 'effective prior to the open of Monday 09-21' is how S&P DJI words a flow that PRINTS AT THE 2026-09-18 CLOSE — index trackers must own the new roster before Monday's open, so the trade is the Friday closing auction, the same auction where triple-witching single-stock options settle. The already-tracked russell-quarterly-ipo-review-effective-2026-09-21 documents the identical geometry in FTSE Russell's own words ('after the close on the third Friday of the month', effective open 09-21); this is the S&P family's leg of the same session, against a materially larger tracking base. ONE CONCRETE ITEM FOR THAT AUCTION: The Trade Desk (TTD) leaves the S&P 500 there — a liquid single-name options underlying whose index-deletion flow lands in the same closing print as its own expiring contracts. IMPACT IS LOW, deliberately, and matches every sibling index-flow entry: this changes execution timing on high-open-interest names, never direction, no house playbook (S1/S2/E1/S3/S4/G1) is opex- or rebalance-keyed, and the sibling Russell research measured the index-flow class as having no index-level effect. Symbols deliberately EMPTY: the flow lives in the individual names entering and leaving, and an ETF proxy would only make the deterministic screen trip on broad-market beta. Kind 'sector' matches the sibling market-structure flow entries; the enum has no index-flow member and the imperfect fit is named here rather than fixed from this lane. WHAT THIS PROPOSAL DOES NOT ESTABLISH: the release publishes MEMBERSHIP only. The share-count and float-adjustment deltas that actually size the 09-18 market-on-close imbalance are in the client-distributed pro-forma files and were not fetched, which is why the opex ledger scores its rebalance kill switch 'not fired on the evidence available' rather than 'cleared'.
